```{r}
# ============================================================
# 1. PACKAGES AND SETTINGS
# ============================================================

# Install if necessary
# install.packages("ranger")
# install.packages("dplyr")
# install.packages("ggplot2")

library(ranger)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(skellam)

# Reproducibility
set.seed(6769)

# Number of trees in each Random Forest
N_TREES <- 1000
```
```{r}
# ============================================================
# 2. TOURNAMENT DATASETS
# ============================================================

euro_data <- list(
  "2004" = euro_2004,
  "2008" = euro_2008,
  "2012" = euro_2012,
  "2016" = euro_2016,
  "2020" = euro_2020,
  "2024" = euro_2024_fixed
)

# Check number of observations per tournament
sapply(euro_data, nrow)

# Check column names
lapply(euro_data, names)

# Combine all tournaments
EuroAll <- bind_rows(euro_data, .id = "Tournament")

# Check dimensions
dim(EuroAll)

# Check tournament distribution
table(EuroAll$Tournament)
```
```{r}
# ============================================================
# 3. RESPONSE AND PREDICTORS
# ============================================================

target <- "Goals"

predictors <- c(
  "GroupStage",
  "GDP",
  "MarketValue",
  "FifaRank",
  "UefaPoints",
  "CLPlayers"
)

# Formula used by all Random Forest models
rf_formula <- as.formula(
  paste(target, "~", paste(predictors, collapse = " + "))
)

# Check that all required columns exist
required_columns <- c(target, predictors)

stopifnot(
  all(required_columns %in% names(EuroAll))
)

# Check missing values
colSums(is.na(EuroAll[, required_columns]))

# Check variable types
str(EuroAll[, required_columns])
```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# 4. EVALUATION METRICS
# ============================================================

calculate_metrics <- function(actual, predicted) {

  # Prevent zero or negative predicted rates
  lambda <- pmax(predicted, 1e-10)

  mae <- mean(abs(actual - predicted))

  rmse <- sqrt(mean((actual - predicted)^2))

  poisson_nll <- -mean(
    dpois(actual, lambda = lambda, log = TRUE)
  )

  return(
    data.frame(
      MAE = mae,
      RMSE = rmse,
      Poisson_NLL = poisson_nll
    )
  )
}
```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# 5. CROSS-VALIDATION FOLDS
# ============================================================

fold_years <- names(euro_data)

# Create a list containing training and validation data
cv_folds <- lapply(fold_years, function(test_year) {

  train_data <- EuroAll %>%
    filter(Tournament != test_year)

  validation_data <- EuroAll %>%
    filter(Tournament == test_year)

  list(
    train = train_data,
    validation = validation_data,
    year = test_year
  )
})

names(cv_folds) <- fold_years

# Check the number of observations in each fold
fold_sizes <- data.frame(
  Tournament = fold_years,
  Training_Observations = sapply(
    cv_folds, function(x) nrow(x$train)
  ),
  Validation_Observations = sapply(
    cv_folds, function(x) nrow(x$validation)
  )
)

print(fold_sizes)
```
```{r}
# ============================================================
# 6. HYPERPARAMETER GRID
# ============================================================

rf_grid <- expand.grid(

  mtry = 1:length(predictors),

  min.node.size = c(3, 5, 10, 15),

  sample.fraction = c(0.7, 0.85, 1.0)

)

# Number of combinations
nrow(rf_grid)

head(rf_grid)
```
```{r}
# ============================================================
# 7. RANDOM FOREST CROSS-VALIDATION
# ============================================================

# Store results for every hyperparameter combination
cv_results <- vector("list", nrow(rf_grid))

for (i in seq_len(nrow(rf_grid))) {

  # Current hyperparameter combination
  params <- rf_grid[i, ]

  # Store metrics for the six folds
  fold_results <- vector("list", length(cv_folds))

  for (j in seq_along(cv_folds)) {

    # Get training and validation data
    train_data <- cv_folds[[j]]$train
    validation_data <- cv_folds[[j]]$validation

    # Fit Random Forest
    set.seed(6769 + i * 10 + j)

    rf_model <- ranger(
      formula = rf_formula,
      data = train_data[, required_columns],
      num.trees = N_TREES,
      mtry = params$mtry,
      min.node.size = params$min.node.size,
      sample.fraction = params$sample.fraction,
      importance = "none",
      seed = 6769 + i * 10 + j
    )

    # Predict on the held-out tournament
    predictions <- predict(
      rf_model,
      data = validation_data[, predictors]
    )$predictions

    # Calculate performance
    metrics <- calculate_metrics(
      validation_data$Goals,
      predictions
    )

    fold_results[[j]] <- data.frame(
      Tournament = cv_folds[[j]]$year,
      MAE = metrics$MAE,
      RMSE = metrics$RMSE,
      Poisson_NLL = metrics$Poisson_NLL
    )
  }

  # Combine results across the six folds
  fold_results_df <- bind_rows(fold_results)

  # Store average performance
  cv_results[[i]] <- data.frame(
    mtry = params$mtry,
    min.node.size = params$min.node.size,
    sample.fraction = params$sample.fraction,
    Mean_MAE = mean(fold_results_df$MAE),
    Mean_RMSE = mean(fold_results_df$RMSE),
    Mean_Poisson_NLL = mean(fold_results_df$Poisson_NLL),
    SD_MAE = sd(fold_results_df$MAE)
  )

  # Progress indicator
  if (i %% 10 == 0 || i == nrow(rf_grid)) {
    cat("Completed", i, "of", nrow(rf_grid), "combinations\n")
  }
}

# Combine all hyperparameter results
cv_results <- bind_rows(cv_results)

# Sort by mean cross-validation MAE
cv_results <- cv_results %>%
  arrange(Mean_MAE)

# Display the 10 best combinations
head(cv_results, 10)
```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# 11. Generate out-of-fold predictions
# ============================================================

oof_predictions <- list()

# Identify the six tournaments
tournaments <- unique(EuroAll$Tournament)

for (j in seq_along(tournaments)) {

  # Select the tournament to hold out
  held_out_tournament <- tournaments[j]

  validation_data <- EuroAll %>%
    filter(Tournament == held_out_tournament)

  # Use all remaining tournaments for training
  training_data <- EuroAll %>%
    filter(Tournament != held_out_tournament)

  # Fit Random Forest using the selected hyperparameters
  rf_model <- ranger(
    formula = rf_formula,
    data = training_data,
    num.trees = N_TREES,
    mtry = best_params$mtry,
    min.node.size = best_params$min.node.size,
    sample.fraction = best_params$sample.fraction,
    importance = "permutation",
    seed = 6769
  )

  # Predict goals for the held-out tournament
  predictions <- predict(
    rf_model,
    data = validation_data
  )$predictions

  # Store predictions, including the unique match identifier
  oof_predictions[[j]] <- data.frame(
    Tournament = validation_data$Tournament,
    match_id = validation_data$match_id,
    Team = as.character(validation_data$Team),
    Opponent = as.character(validation_data$Opponent),
    Goals = validation_data$Goals,
    PredictedGoals = predictions
  )
}

# Combine predictions from all six tournaments
oof_predictions <- bind_rows(oof_predictions)

# Check the results
names(oof_predictions)
dim(oof_predictions)

# Verify that every observation received a prediction
stopifnot(
  nrow(oof_predictions) == nrow(EuroAll),
  !any(is.na(oof_predictions$PredictedGoals))
)

# ============================================================
# 12. Aggregate predictions into individual matches
# ============================================================

match_data <- oof_predictions %>%
  mutate(
    Team = as.character(Team),
    Opponent = as.character(Opponent),

    # Establish a consistent ordering of the two teams
    Team1_name = pmin(Team, Opponent),
    Team2_name = pmax(Team, Opponent),

    # Identify which observation corresponds to Team 1
    Is_Team1 = Team == Team1_name
  ) %>%
  group_by(Tournament, match_id) %>%
  summarise(
    N_Teams = n(),

    Team1 = first(Team1_name),
    Team2 = first(Team2_name),

    # Actual goals scored
    Goals1 = first(Goals[Is_Team1]),
    Goals2 = first(Goals[!Is_Team1]),

    # Random Forest predicted goals
    Lambda1 = first(PredictedGoals[Is_Team1]),
    Lambda2 = first(PredictedGoals[!Is_Team1]),

    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Verify that every match has exactly two team observations
table(match_data$N_Teams)

stopifnot(all(match_data$N_Teams == 2))

# Inspect the resulting match-level dataset
dim(match_data)
head(match_data, 10)
```
```{r}
# ============================================================
# 13. Calculate Win, Draw and Loss Probabilities
# ============================================================


match_data <- match_data %>%
  mutate(
    # Ensure strictly positive Poisson rates
    Lambda1 = pmax(Lambda1, 1e-10),
    Lambda2 = pmax(Lambda2, 1e-10),

    # Probability that Team 1 wins
    P_Win = skellam::pskellam(
      0, Lambda1, Lambda2,
      lower.tail = FALSE
    ),

    # Probability of a draw
    P_Draw = skellam::dskellam(
      0, Lambda1, Lambda2
    ),

    # Probability that Team 1 loses
    P_Loss = skellam::pskellam(
      -1, Lambda1, Lambda2
    ),

    # Sum of the three probabilities (should equal 1)
    Probability_Sum = P_Win + P_Draw + P_Loss
  )

# Inspect the calculated probabilities
match_data %>%
  select(
    Tournament, Team1, Team2,
    Lambda1, Lambda2,
    P_Win, P_Draw, P_Loss,
    Probability_Sum
  ) %>%
  head(10)

# Verify that all probabilities are valid
stopifnot(
  all(match_data$P_Win >= 0 & match_data$P_Win <= 1),
  all(match_data$P_Draw >= 0 & match_data$P_Draw <= 1),
  all(match_data$P_Loss >= 0 & match_data$P_Loss <= 1),
  all(abs(match_data$Probability_Sum - 1) < 1e-8)
)

# Summary of probability sums
summary(match_data$Probability_Sum)
```
```{r}
# ============================================================
# 14. Grid Search for the Draw Classification Threshold
# ============================================================

# 1. Determine actual match outcomes from observed goals

match_data <- match_data %>%
  mutate(
    Actual_Outcome = case_when(
      Goals1 > Goals2 ~ "Win",
      Goals1 == Goals2 ~ "Draw",
      Goals1 < Goals2 ~ "Loss"
    ),

    Actual_Outcome = factor(
      Actual_Outcome,
      levels = c("Win", "Draw", "Loss")
    )
  )


# 2. Define candidate thresholds

threshold_grid <- c(0.05, 0.10, 0.15, 0.20, 0.25)


# 3. Construct probability matrix

prob_matrix <- as.matrix(
  match_data[, c("P_Win", "P_Draw", "P_Loss")]
)

colnames(prob_matrix) <- c("Win", "Draw", "Loss")


# 4. Calculate probability range for each match

Probability_Range <- apply(prob_matrix, 1, max) -
                     apply(prob_matrix, 1, min)


# 5. Determine outcome with highest probability

Max_Probability_Outcome <- c("Win", "Draw", "Loss")[
  max.col(prob_matrix, ties.method = "first")
]


# 6. Evaluate classification accuracy for each threshold

threshold_results <- data.frame(
  Threshold = threshold_grid,
  Accuracy = sapply(threshold_grid, function(threshold) {

    Predicted_Outcome <- ifelse(
      Probability_Range < threshold,
      "Draw",
      Max_Probability_Outcome
    )

    mean(
      Predicted_Outcome == as.character(match_data$Actual_Outcome)
    )
  })
)


# 7. Display threshold comparison

print(threshold_results)


# 8. Select threshold with highest accuracy

best_threshold <- threshold_results$Threshold[
  which.max(threshold_results$Accuracy)
]

cat("\nBest threshold:", best_threshold, "\n")
cat("Best accuracy:", max(threshold_results$Accuracy), "\n")


# 9. Apply optimal threshold to all matches

match_data <- match_data %>%
  mutate(
    Probability_Range = Probability_Range,

    Predicted_Outcome = ifelse(
      Probability_Range < best_threshold,
      "Draw",
      Max_Probability_Outcome
    ),

    Predicted_Outcome = factor(
      Predicted_Outcome,
      levels = c("Win", "Draw", "Loss")
    )
  )


# 10. Inspect predictions

match_data %>%
  select(
    Tournament, Team1, Team2,
    Goals1, Goals2,
    P_Win, P_Draw, P_Loss,
    Probability_Range,
    Actual_Outcome, Predicted_Outcome
  ) %>%
  head(15)


# 11. Compare actual and predicted outcome frequencies

table(match_data$Actual_Outcome)
table(match_data$Predicted_Outcome)
```

```{r}
# ============================================================
# 16. Baseline Model: Historical Outcome Frequencies
# ============================================================

outcome_levels <- c("Win", "Draw", "Loss")

baseline_predictions <- match_data %>%
  select(Tournament, Actual_Outcome) %>%
  mutate(
    P_Win = NA_real_,
    P_Draw = NA_real_,
    P_Loss = NA_real_
  )

tournaments <- unique(match_data$Tournament)

for (t in tournaments) {

  # Outcomes from the other five tournaments
  training_outcomes <- match_data$Actual_Outcome[
    match_data$Tournament != t
  ]

  # Historical outcome probabilities
  outcome_probs <- prop.table(
    table(factor(
      as.character(training_outcomes),
      levels = outcome_levels
    ))
  )

  # Assign probabilities to the held-out tournament
  idx <- which(baseline_predictions$Tournament == t)

  baseline_predictions$P_Win[idx] <- outcome_probs["Win"]
  baseline_predictions$P_Draw[idx] <- outcome_probs["Draw"]
  baseline_predictions$P_Loss[idx] <- outcome_probs["Loss"]
}

# Construct baseline probability matrix
baseline_matrix <- as.matrix(
  baseline_predictions[, c("P_Win", "P_Draw", "P_Loss")]
)

colnames(baseline_matrix) <- outcome_levels

# Actual outcome indices
actual_index <- match(
  as.character(baseline_predictions$Actual_Outcome),
  outcome_levels
)

# Probability assigned to the actual outcome
baseline_true_probs <- baseline_matrix[
  cbind(seq_len(nrow(baseline_matrix)), actual_index)
]

# Baseline log loss
baseline_log_loss <- -mean(
  log(pmax(baseline_true_probs, 1e-15))
)

# One-hot encoded actual outcomes
baseline_actual_matrix <- matrix(
  0,
  nrow = nrow(baseline_matrix),
  ncol = 3
)

baseline_actual_matrix[
  cbind(seq_len(nrow(baseline_matrix)), actual_index)
] <- 1

# Baseline Brier score
baseline_brier_score <- mean(
  rowSums((baseline_matrix - baseline_actual_matrix)^2)
)

# Baseline predicted classes
baseline_predicted <- factor(
  outcome_levels[max.col(baseline_matrix, ties.method = "first")],
  levels = outcome_levels
)

# Baseline accuracy
baseline_accuracy <- mean(
  baseline_predicted == baseline_predictions$Actual_Outcome
)

# Compare Random Forest against baseline
model_comparison <- data.frame(
  Model = c("Random Forest + Skellam", "Historical Frequency Baseline"),
  Log_Loss = c(log_loss, baseline_log_loss),
  Brier_Score = c(brier_score, baseline_brier_score),
  Accuracy = c(accuracy, baseline_accuracy)
)

print(model_comparison)
```

# ============================================================
# 17. Visualisation of Predicted Match Probabilities
# ============================================================

library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)

# Convert probability columns into long format
probability_long <- match_data %>%
  select(P_Win, P_Draw, P_Loss) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "Outcome",
    values_to = "Probability"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Outcome = recode(
      Outcome,
      P_Win = "Win",
      P_Draw = "Draw",
      P_Loss = "Loss"
    ),
    Outcome = factor(
      Outcome,
      levels = c("Win", "Draw", "Loss")
    )
  )

# Plot probability distributions
ggplot(probability_long,
       aes(x = Probability, fill = Outcome)) +
  geom_histogram(
    bins = 25,
    alpha = 0.75,
    color = "white"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~Outcome, ncol = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Predicted Match Outcome Probabilities",
    x = "Predicted Probability",
    y = "Number of Matches"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

# ============================================================
# 17.3 Average Predicted Probabilities vs Actual Frequencies
# ============================================================

probability_comparison <- data.frame(
  Outcome = factor(
    c("Win", "Draw", "Loss"),
    levels = c("Win", "Draw", "Loss")
  ),
  Mean_Predicted_Probability = c(
    mean(match_data$P_Win),
    mean(match_data$P_Draw),
    mean(match_data$P_Loss)
  ),
  Actual_Frequency = c(
    mean(match_data$Actual_Outcome == "Win"),
    mean(match_data$Actual_Outcome == "Draw"),
    mean(match_data$Actual_Outcome == "Loss")
  )
)

probability_comparison_long <- probability_comparison %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Mean_Predicted_Probability, Actual_Frequency),
    names_to = "Measure",
    values_to = "Probability"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Measure = recode(
      Measure,
      Mean_Predicted_Probability = "Mean Predicted Probability",
      Actual_Frequency = "Actual Frequency"
    )
  )

ggplot(
  probability_comparison_long,
  aes(x = Outcome, y = Probability, fill = Measure)
) +
  geom_col(
    position = "dodge",
    width = 0.7
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Average Predicted Probabilities vs Actual Frequencies",
    x = "Match Outcome",
    y = "Probability",
    fill = "Measure"

  theme_minimal()
